newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilts end down on fears of bond sale by RBI.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilts end down on fears of bond sale by RBI.

text.p: Prices of Indian government securities ended down in moderate trade on Thursday on fears the central bank would sell newly issued 10-year bonds at prices below current market rates, dealers said.
The Indian government on Wednesday placed 50 billion rupees of 10-year bonds with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at 13.05 percent against secondary market yields of 12.60.
They said the market turned bearish on fears the yield would realign itself on sale of the new bond by the RBI.

"Basically it (the drop in prices) was driven by sentiment," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Had the RBI put the new bond on its sale window, there would have been a real crash in long bond prices."
Dealers said the market stabilised after it became clear the RBI was not selling the 10-year bond on Thursday.
"The 13.05 percent 2007 fell to 101 rupees today against yesterday's 101.95 before recovering to 101.25 later in the day," said a dealer.

Among other stocks, the 13.40 percent 1998 fell to 103.70 rupees from 104.20, the 13.62 percent 1998 to 105.50 from 106, the 13.40 percent 1999 to 107.65 from 107.90 and the 13.70 percent 1999 to 107.52 from 107.90.
Dealers said market focus seemed to have shifted to medium-term stocks and volumes came down from Wednesday's level.
Trades on the National Stock Exchange were worth 4.2 billion rupees on Thursday against Wednesday's 7.14, dealers said.
Dealers said call money rates ended unchanged from opening levels at 0.10-0.25 percent in conditions of good liquidity and poor demand.
Dealers said three-month term money was traded at 9.0 percent.
Three-month commercial paper was quoted at 10.0-10.5 percent in the primary market, dealers said.
In the secondary market, one-month commercial paper was traded at 8.35 percent.
In certificates of deposit (CDs), a 45-day CD was traded in the secondary market at 6.75 percent, dealers said.
One-month CDs were quoted at 6.0 percent and two-month Cds at 7.5 in the secondary market, dealers said.
